messages.author: 00372e5d281e2963
messages.subject: Custom HTML layout / Bootstrap theming
parts:
Hi,

Apologies in advance if the post is unclear, but this is an area that is very nebulous to me in the first place. This is about the styling of an application, and i have no experience at all in that area.

So, i've been writing a Shiny application, and the functionality is fine. The ui.R sets a basic layout with all the static pieces, as well as a number of plot, data and UI widgets which are dynamically generated in the server.R.

The users of the applications would now like to have it themed to company colours and be generally more visually pleasant. To that end, a designer produced a full set of assets for Bootstrap, on the basis that Shiny was using Bootstrap to produce its HTML, and supported standalone Bootstrap CSS files. I'm now presented with a large set of assets including CSS files, JS files, images, fonts, etc. And i'm a bit at a loss as to whether this can be used by Shiny at all. I'm not a web developer at all, and looks-wise, all i can do so far is include a CSS stylesheet (through "theme='mytheme.css'" or through manual tags in the header), which works as expected, and styles whatever elements the CSS specifies. But that's clearly not enough in this case, as i'm facing multiple CSS files and other types of web assets.

The theme designer tells me that he wrote custom HTML layouts, and that these would need to be used by the application. These contain mobile-friendly layouts among other things. Basically, he custom built a HTML structure that he would like the application to use. But the way i've been using Shiny so far, i've always left it generate its own HTML, apart from when i injected a few elements manually here and there within a UI output.

So my questions are twofold:
- Is that possible?
- What does it involve? Would it mean scrapping the ui.R and mapping each element from the HTML files to server.R elements? How can i get a renderUI() output from server.R to appear in a static HTML page for example?

I'm happy to clarify as much as i can if this is unclear. Again, i've got no knowledge or experience on the web development side, something that Shiny has been sheltering me from until now.

Regards,
Bruno.

messages.subject: Re: Custom HTML layout / Bootstrap theming
parts:
Hi Joe,

Many thanks for that. I gave a try at the templates, and this is a lovely approach. It works brilliantly on the first page of the application (an index.html) which i use as the template.

The trouble now is that this first page contains links to other html pages, each one a different part of the application. Right now my files are stored a bit like this:

shinyapp/
\--- ui.R
\--- server.R
\--- index.html
\--- www/
       \---secondpage.html
       \---thirdpage.html

And index.html contains a plain <href> link to secondpage.html and thirdpage.html which are full self-contained documents, with their own header and content. And they should also contain some shiny widgets.

Right now, the link works since the files are in the www/ folder, but on loading them, the styling breaks up badly, and i can't use template code in them as far as i understand. Is there a way to define multiple pages as templates?

Cheers,
Bruno.
